prompt: Our NestJS API tags every log line with a per-request correlation id so we can trace a single request's logs end-to-end. `RequestContextService` holds the current `requestId`, `RequestContextMiddleware` stamps a fresh UUID onto it at the start of each request, and the logger reads it back through that same service on every log call. It works perfectly on your laptop and in our single-request integration tests — but in production, under real concurrent traffic, log lines start showing the WRONG requestId: request A's logs get tagged with request B's id, and correlation across a request breaks. Look at the code below, find why the shared context leaks across concurrent requests, explain why serial testing never catches it, and tell me how you'd fix it without abandoning this single shared logging pipeline.
